1	# Zitadel Migration Implementation Plan
2	
3	> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
4	
5	**Goal:** Replace Keycloak with Zitadel as the identity provider, add Cloudflare Tunnels for routing, update Go backend JWT middleware, and rebuild the Vue frontend auth flow with a 2-step onboarding wizard.
6	
7	**Architecture:** Three-phase sequential migration: (1) Infrastructure — swap Docker Compose services, (2) Backend — replace JWT middleware and provisioning endpoints, (3) Frontend — swap OIDC client and rebuild onboarding. Zitadel handles identity only; Raven continues to manage multi-tenancy via PostgreSQL RLS.
8	
9	**Tech Stack:** Zitadel v2.71.12, `github.com/zitadel/oidc/v3` (Go), `oidc-client-ts` (Vue), Cloudflare Tunnels (`cloudflared`), PostgreSQL 18, Gin, Vue 3 + Pinia.
10	
11	**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-13-zitadel-migration-design.md`
12	
13	---
14

19	    ## Before You Begin
20	
21	    If you have questions about:
22	    - The requirements or acceptance criteria
23	    - The approach or implementation strategy
24	    - Dependencies or assumptions
25	    - Anything unclear in the task description
26	
27	    **Ask them now.** Raise any concerns before starting work.
28	
29	    ## Your Job
30	
31	    Once you're clear on requirements:
32	    1. Implement exactly what the task specifies
33	    2. Write tests (following TDD if task says to)
34	    3. Verify implementation works
35	    4. Commit your work
36	    5. Self-review (see below)
37	    6. Report back
38	
39	    Work from: [directory]
40	
41	    **While you work:** If you encounter something unexpected or unclear, **ask questions**.
42	    It's always OK to pause and clarify. Don't guess or make assumptions.
43	
44	    ## Code Organization
45	
46	    You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more
47	    reliable when files are focused. Keep this in mind:
48	    - Follow the file structure defined in the plan
49	    - Each file should have one clear responsibility with a well-defined interface
50	    - If a file you're creating is growing beyond the plan's intent, stop and report
51	      it as DONE_WITH_CONCERNS — don't split files on your own without plan guidance
52	    - If an existing file you're modifying is already large or tangled, work carefully
53	      and note it as a concern in your report
54	    - In existing codebases, follow established patterns. Improve code you're touching
55	      the way a good developer would, but don't restructure things outside your task.
56	
57	    ## When You're in Over Your Head
58	
59	    It is always OK to stop and say "this is too hard for me." Bad work is worse than
60	    no work. You will not be penalized for escalating.
61	
62	    **STOP and escalate when:**
63	    - The task requires architectural decisions with multiple valid approaches
64	    - You need to understand code beyond what was provided and can't find clarity
65	    - You feel uncertain about whether your approach is correct
66	    - The task involves restructuring existing code in ways the plan didn't anticipate
67	    - You've been reading file after file trying to understand the system without progress
68	
69	    **How to escalate:** Report back with status BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT. Describe
70	    specifically what you're stuck on, what you've tried, and what kind of help you need.
71	    The controller can provide more context, re-dispatch with a more capable model,
72	    or break the task into smaller pieces.
73	
74	    ## Before Reporting Back: Self-Review
75	
76	    Review your work with fresh eyes. Ask yourself:
77	
78	    **Completeness:**
79	    - Did I fully implement everything in the spec?
80	    - Did I miss any requirements?
81	    - Are there edge cases I didn't handle?
82	
83	    **Quality:**
84	    - Is this my best work?
85	    - Are names clear and accurate (match what things do, not how they work)?
86	    - Is the code clean and maintainable?
87	
88	    **Discipline:**
89	    - Did I avoid overbuilding (YAGNI)?
90	    - Did I only build what was requested?
91	    - Did I follow existing patterns in the codebase?
92	
93	    **Testing:**
94	    - Do tests actually verify behavior (not just mock behavior)?
95	    - Did I follow TDD if required?
96	    - Are tests comprehensive?
97	
98	    If you find issues during self-review, fix them now before reporting.
99	
100	    ## Report Format
101	
102	    When done, report:
103	    - **Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT
104	    - What you implemented (or what you attempted, if blocked)
105	    - What you tested and test results
106	    - Files changed
107	    - Self-review findings (if any)
108	    - Any issues or concerns
109	
110	    Use DONE_WITH_CONCERNS if you completed the work but have doubts about correctness.
111	    Use BLOCKED if you cannot complete the task. Use NEEDS_CONTEXT if you need
112	    information that wasn't provided. Never silently produce work you're unsure about.
113	```

760	Replace `frontend/src/stores/auth.ts` entirely. The new store uses `oidc-client-ts`:
761	
762	```typescript
763	import { defineStore } from 'pinia'
764	import { UserManager, WebStorageStateStore } from 'oidc-client-ts'
765	import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
766	
767	const userManager = new UserManager({
768	  authority: import.meta.env.VITE_ZITADEL_URL,
769	  client_id: import.meta.env.VITE_ZITADEL_CLIENT_ID,
770	  redirect_uri: `${window.location.origin}/callback`,
771	  post_logout_redirect_uri: window.location.origin,
772	  silent_redirect_uri: `${window.location.origin}/silent-renew.html`,
773	  scope: 'openid profile email',
774	  response_type: 'code',
775	  automaticSilentRenew: true,
776	  userStore: new WebStorageStateStore({ store: window.sessionStorage }),
777	})
778	
779	export const useAuthStore = defineStore('auth', () => {
780	  const user = ref(null)
781	  const orgId = ref(null)
782	  const isAuthenticated = computed(() => !!user.value)
783	  const hasOrg = computed(() => !!orgId.value)
784	  const accessToken = computed(() => user.value?.access_token)
785	
786	  async function init() {
787	    const existingUser = await userManager.getUser()
788	    if (existingUser && !existingUser.expired) {
789	      user.value = existingUser
790	    }
791	  }
792	
793	  async function login(idpHint?: string) {
794	    const extraParams = idpHint ? { idp_hint: idpHint } : {}
795	    await userManager.signinRedirect({ extraQueryParams: extraParams })
796	  }
797	
798	  async function handleCallback() {
799	    const callbackUser = await userManager.signinRedirectCallback()
800	    user.value = callbackUser
801	    return callbackUser
802	  }
803	
804	  async function logout() {
805	    await userManager.signoutRedirect()
806	    user.value = null
807	    orgId.value = null
808	  }
809	
810	  function setOrgId(id: string) {
811	    orgId.value = id
812	  }
813	
814	  return { user, orgId, isAuthenticated, hasOrg, accessToken, init, login, handleCallback, logout, setOrgId }
815	})
816	```

## keycloak service block in docker-compose

### docker-compose.yml (1)
# docker-compose.yml

services:
  # ─── Go API ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  go-api:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      # OpenTelemetry — ship traces, metrics and logs to OpenObserve.
      RAVEN_OTEL_ENABLED: "true"
      RAVEN_OTEL_ENDPOINT: "openobserve:5081"
      RAVEN_OTEL_SERVICE_NAME: "raven-api"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      valkey:
        condition: service_healthy
      keycloak:
        condition: service_started
      openobserve:
        condition: service_started
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:8080/healthz"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 10s
    networks:
      - raven-internal
    labels:
      - "traefik.enable=true"
      # ── HTTP → HTTPS redirect is handled globally by Traefik entrypoint config ──
      # ── HTTPS router ──
      - "traefik.http.routers.api.rule=Host(`${RAVEN_DOMAIN:-localhost}`) && PathPrefix(`/api`)"
      - "traefik.http.routers.api.entrypoints=websecure"
      - "traefik.http.routers.api.tls=true"
      - "traefik.http.routers.api.tls.certresolver=${TRAEFIK_CERT_RESOLVER:-letsencrypt}"
      - "traefik.http.routers.api.middlewares=security-headers@file"
      - "traefik.http.services.api.loadbalancer.server.port=8080"
    restart: unless-stopped
    # eBPF capabilities (CAP_BPF, CAP_NET_ADMIN) are in docker-compose.ebpf.yml overlay

  # ─── Python AI Worker (gRPC) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  python-worker:
    build:
      context: ./ai-worker
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      RAVEN_MEMORY_DIR: /var/raven/memories
    volumes:
      - raven-memories:/var/raven/memories
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      valkey:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      - raven-internal
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ─── Python Voice Agent (LiveKit) ─────────────────────────────────────────
  python-agent:
    build:
      context: ./ai-worker
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      RAVEN_LIVEKIT_URL: ws://livekit-server:7880
      RAVEN_LIVEKIT_API_KEY: ${LIVEKIT_API_KEY:-devkey}
      RAVEN_LIVEKIT_API_SECRET: ${LIVEKIT_API_SECRET:-devsecret}
    command: ["python", "-m", "raven_worker.agent"]
    depends_on:
      livekit-server:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      - raven-internal
    restart: unless-stopped

### docker-compose.yml (4)
# ─── OpenObserve (Observability) ───────────────────────────────────────────
  openobserve:
    image: public.ecr.aws/zinclabs/openobserve:latest
    ports:
      - "5080:5080"   # UI + HTTP API
      - "5081:5081"   # gRPC OTLP receiver (traces, metrics, logs)
    environment:
      ZO_ROOT_USER_EMAIL: ${ZO_ROOT_USER_EMAIL:-admin@raven.local}
      ZO_ROOT_USER_PASSWORD: ${ZO_ROOT_USER_PASSWORD:?ZO_ROOT_USER_PASSWORD is required}
      # Enable OTLP gRPC ingestion on port 5081.
      ZO_GRPC_PORT: "5081"
    volumes:
      - openobserve-data:/data
    networks:
      - raven-internal
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ─── pgBackRest Backup Sidecar ────────────────────────────────────────────
  pgbackrest:
    image: pgbackrest/pgbackrest:latest
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      PGBACKREST_STANZA: raven
      PGBACKREST_PG1_HOST: postgres
      PGBACKREST_PG1_PORT: "5432"
      PGBACKREST_PG1_DATABASE: ${POSTGRES_DB:-raven}
    volumes:
      - ./backup/pgbackrest.conf:/etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf:ro
      - ./backup/backup.sh:/backup/backup.sh:ro
      - ./backup/restore.sh:/backup/restore.sh:ro
      - pg-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data:ro
      - pgbackrest-repo:/var/lib/pgbackrest
      - pgbackrest-log:/var/log/pgbackrest
    networks:
      - raven-internal
    # Keep container running so exec works for on-demand backups
    command: ["sleep", "infinity"]
    restart: unless-stopped

## keycloak database creation in init.sql

### deploy/postgres/init.sql
# deploy/postgres/init.sql

-- Raven PostgreSQL initialisation
-- Runs once when the data volume is first created.

-- Keycloak needs its own database
SELECT 'CREATE DATABASE keycloak'
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'keycloak')\gexec

CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "uuid-ossp";
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "vector";
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "pg_trgm";

-- Voice session enums (added in migration 00029)
DO $$ BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_type WHERE typname = 'voice_session_state') THEN
        CREATE TYPE voice_session_state AS ENUM ('created', 'active', 'ended');
    END IF;
END $$;

DO $$ BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_type WHERE typname = 'voice_speaker') THEN
        CREATE TYPE voice_speaker AS ENUM ('agent', 'user');
    END IF;
END $$;

-- WhatsApp-LiveKit bridge table (added for issue #67)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS whatsapp_bridges (
    id               UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),
    org_id           UUID NOT NULL,
    call_id          TEXT NOT NULL,
    livekit_room     TEXT NOT NULL,
    bridge_state     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'initializing',
    voice_session_id UUID,
    sdp_offer        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    sdp_answer       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    metadata         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    created_at       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    closed_at        TIMESTAMPTZ,
    UNIQUE (org_id, call_id)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_whatsapp_bridges_org_state
    ON whatsapp_bridges (org_id, bridge_state)
    WHERE bridge_state IN ('initializing', 'active');

  seaweedfs-volume:
    image: chrislusf/seaweedfs
    command: "volume -mserver=seaweedfs-master:9333 -ip.bind=0.0.0.0 -dir=/data"
    volumes:
      - seaweedfs-data:/data
    depends_on:
      - seaweedfs-master
    networks:
      - raven-internal
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ─── SeaweedFS Filer (S3 API) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  seaweedfs-filer:
    image: chrislusf/seaweedfs
    command: "filer -master=seaweedfs-master:9333 -ip.bind=0.0.0.0 -s3"
    ports:
      - "8888:8888"
    depends_on:
      - seaweedfs-master
      - seaweedfs-volume
    networks:
      - raven-internal
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ─── Traefik Reverse Proxy ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  traefik:
    image: traefik:v3.3
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
      - "8082:8080"
    environment:
      # DNS-01 challenge provider credentials — set in .env
      ACME_EMAIL: ${ACME_EMAIL:-admin@raven.local}
      ACME_DNS_PROVIDER: ${ACME_DNS_PROVIDER:-cloudflare}
      ACME_CA_SERVER: ${ACME_CA_SERVER:-https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory}
      # Provider-specific credentials (Cloudflare example)
      CF_API_EMAIL: ${CF_API_EMAIL:-}
      CF_DNS_API_TOKEN: ${CF_DNS_API_TOKEN:-}
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - ./deploy/traefik/traefik.yml:/etc/traefik/traefik.yml:ro
      - ./deploy/traefik/dynamic:/etc/traefik/dynamic:ro
      - acme-data:/acme
    networks:
      - raven-internal
    restart: unless-stopped

### docker-compose.yml (1)
# docker-compose.yml

services:
  # ─── Go API ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  go-api:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      # OpenTelemetry — ship traces, metrics and logs to OpenObserve.
      RAVEN_OTEL_ENABLED: "true"
      RAVEN_OTEL_ENDPOINT: "openobserve:5081"
      RAVEN_OTEL_SERVICE_NAME: "raven-api"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      valkey:
        condition: service_healthy
      keycloak:
        condition: service_started
      openobserve:
        condition: service_started
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:8080/healthz"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 10s
    networks:
      - raven-internal
    labels:
      - "traefik.enable=true"
      # ── HTTP → HTTPS redirect is handled globally by Traefik entrypoint config ──
      # ── HTTPS router ──
      - "traefik.http.routers.api.rule=Host(`${RAVEN_DOMAIN:-localhost}`) && PathPrefix(`/api`)"
      - "traefik.http.routers.api.entrypoints=websecure"
      - "traefik.http.routers.api.tls=true"
      - "traefik.http.routers.api.tls.certresolver=${TRAEFIK_CERT_RESOLVER:-letsencrypt}"
      - "traefik.http.routers.api.middlewares=security-headers@file"
      - "traefik.http.services.api.loadbalancer.server.port=8080"
    restart: unless-stopped
    # eBPF capabilities (CAP_BPF, CAP_NET_ADMIN) are in docker-compose.ebpf.yml overlay

  # ─── Python AI Worker (gRPC) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  python-worker:
    build:
      context: ./ai-worker
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      RAVEN_MEMORY_DIR: /var/raven/memories
    volumes:
      - raven-memories:/var/raven/memories
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      valkey:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      - raven-internal
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ─── Python Voice Agent (LiveKit) ─────────────────────────────────────────
  python-agent:
    build:
      context: ./ai-worker
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      RAVEN_LIVEKIT_URL: ws://livekit-server:7880
      RAVEN_LIVEKIT_API_KEY: ${LIVEKIT_API_KEY:-devkey}
      RAVEN_LIVEKIT_API_SECRET: ${LIVEKIT_API_SECRET:-devsecret}
    command: ["python", "-m", "raven_worker.agent"]
    depends_on:
      livekit-server:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      - raven-internal
    restart: unless-stopped

47		jwt.RegisteredClaims
48	
49		// Custom Keycloak / Raven claims.
50		OrgID          string   `json:"org_id"`
51		OrgRole        string   `json:"org_role"`
52		WorkspaceIDs   []string `json:"workspace_ids"`
53		KBPermissions  []string `json:"kb_permissions"`

62	// jwksCache wraps a keyfunc.Keyfunc with TTL-based refresh logic.
63	type jwksCache struct {
64		mu          sync.RWMutex
65		keyfunc     keyfunc.Keyfunc
66		lastRefresh time.Time
67		jwksURL     string
68	}
69	
70	// newJWKSCache creates a new cache and performs an initial fetch.
71	func newJWKSCache(jwksURL string) (*jwksCache, error) {
72		c := &jwksCache{jwksURL: jwksURL}
73		if err := c.refresh(); err != nil {
74			return nil, fmt.Errorf("initial JWKS fetch failed: %w", err)
75		}
76		return c, nil
77	}
78	
79	// refresh fetches the JWKS from the remote endpoint and replaces the cached keyfunc.
80	// A 10-second timeout is applied to the fetch to prevent indefinite blocking.
81	func (c *jwksCache) refresh() error {
82		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
83		defer cancel()
84	
85		kf, err := keyfunc.NewDefaultCtx(ctx, []string{c.jwksURL})
86		if err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		c.mu.Lock()
90		c.keyfunc = kf
91		c.lastRefresh = time.Now()
92		c.mu.Unlock()
93		return nil
94	}
95	
96	// keyFunc returns the jwt.Keyfunc, refreshing the cache if TTL has elapsed or
97	// if forceRefresh is true.
98	func (c *jwksCache) keyFunc(forceRefresh bool) jwt.Keyfunc {
99		c.mu.RLock()
100		expired := time.Since(c.lastRefresh) > jwksCacheTTL
101		kf := c.keyfunc
102		c.mu.RUnlock()
103	
104		if forceRefresh || expired {
105			// Refresh in place; log any error but continue with stale keys.
106			if err := c.refresh(); err != nil {
107				log.Printf("[WARN] JWT middleware: JWKS refresh from %s failed: %v — continuing with cached keys", c.jwksURL, err)
108			}
109			c.mu.RLock()
110			kf = c.keyfunc
111			c.mu.RUnlock()
112		}
113	
114		return kf.Keyfunc
115	}
116	
117	// JWTMiddleware returns a Gin handler that validates Bearer JWTs against the
118	// Keycloak JWKS endpoint, or stubs through API-key requests.
119	//
120	// The middleware is intended to be applied per route-group, not globally.
121	//
122	// On success, the following values are stored in the Gin context:
123	//
124	//	ContextKeyUserID        → string (JWT sub)
125	//	ContextKeyOrgID         → string
126	//	ContextKeyOrgRole       → string
127	//	ContextKeyWorkspaceIDs  → []string
128	//	ContextKeyKBPermissions → []string
129	//	ContextKeyEmail         → string
130	//	ContextKeyClaims        → *Claims
131	//
132	// NOTE: RLS enforcement (`SET LOCAL app.current_org_id`) must be applied by
133	// the repository layer after retrieving ContextKeyOrgID from the context,
134	// because the DB connection is not accessible here.
135	func JWTMiddleware(cfg *config.KeycloakConfig) gin.HandlerFunc {
136		jwksURL := cfg.IssuerURL + "/protocol/openid-connect/certs"
137	
138		const maxAttempts = 3
139		var (
140			cache *jwksCache
141			err   error
142		)
143		for attempt := 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++ {
144			cache, err = newJWKSCache(jwksURL)
145			if err == nil {
146				break
147			}
148			log.Printf("[WARN] JWT middleware: JWKS fetch attempt %d/%d from %s failed: %v", attempt, maxAttempts, jwksURL, err)
149			if attempt < maxAttempts {
150				time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)
151			}
152		}
153		if err != nil {
154			// All attempts exhausted — serve 503 on every protected request until restart.
155			log.Printf("[ERROR] JWT middleware: all %d JWKS fetch attempts failed; all protected endpoints will return 503", maxAttempts)
156			return func(c *gin.Context) {
157				c.AbortWithStatusJSON(http.StatusServiceUnavailable, authError{Error: "jwks_unavailable"})
158			}
159		}
160	
161		return func(c *gin.Context) {
162			// --- Detect auth method ---
163			if apiKey := c.GetHeader("X-API-Key"); apiKey != "" {
164				if !cfg.APIKeyEnabled {
165					abortUnauthorized(c, "api_key_auth_disabled")
166					return
167				}
168				handleAPIKey(c, apiKey)
169				return
170			}
171	
172			authHeader := c.GetHeader("Authorization")
173			if authHeader == "" {
174				abortUnauthorized(c, "missing_token")
175				return
176			}
177	
178			parts := strings.SplitN(authHeader, " ", 2)
179			if len(parts) != 2 || !strings.EqualFold(parts[0], "Bearer") {
180				abortUnauthorized(c, "missing_token")
181				return
182			}
183			rawToken := parts[1]
184	
185			// --- Parse & validate JWT ---
186			claims, err := parseJWT(rawToken, cfg.IssuerURL, cfg.Audience, cache, false)
187			if err != nil {
188				// On any key-related error, retry once with a forced JWKS refresh
189				// (handles key rotation / cache staleness).
190				if isKeyError(err) {
191					claims, err = parseJWT(rawToken, cfg.IssuerURL, cfg.Audience, cache, true)
192				}
193				if err != nil {
194					abortWithTokenError(c, err)
195					return
196				}
197			}
198	
199			// --- Store claims in Gin context ---
200			c.Set(string(ContextKeyUserID), claims.Subject)
201			c.Set(string(ContextKeyOrgID), claims.OrgID)
202			c.Set(string(ContextKeyOrgRole), claims.OrgRole)
203			c.Set(string(ContextKeyWorkspaceIDs), claims.WorkspaceIDs)
204			c.Set(string(ContextKeyKBPermissions), claims.KBPermissions)
205			c.Set(string(ContextKeyEmail), claims.Email)
206			c.Set(string(ContextKeyClaims), claims)
207	
208			c.Next()
209		}
210	}
211	
212	// parseJWT validates the raw token string and returns the parsed Claims.
213	// It validates the issuer, audience, and expiry claims in addition to the signature.
214	func parseJWT(rawToken, issuerURL, audience string, cache *jwksCache, forceRefresh bool) (*Claims, error) {
215		claims := &Claims{}
216		_, err := jwt.ParseWithClaims(
217			rawToken,
218			claims,
219			cache.keyFunc(forceRefresh),
220			jwt.WithIssuer(issuerURL),
221			jwt.WithAudience(audience),
222			jwt.WithExpirationRequired(),
223			jwt.WithLeeway(5*time.Second),
224		)
225		if err != nil {
226			return nil, err
227		}
228		return claims, nil
229	}
230	
231	// isKeyError reports whether the error is likely caused by an unknown/unresolvable
232	// key or a stale key (suggesting a JWKS rotation rather than a malformed token).
233	// ErrTokenSignatureInvalid is included because a key rotation can produce it when
234	// the cached JWKS is stale.
235	func isKeyError(err error) bool {
236		return strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unable to find") ||
237			errors.Is(err, jwt.ErrTokenUnverifiable) ||
238			errors.Is(err, jwt.ErrTokenSignatureInvalid)
239	}
240	
241	// abortWithTokenError maps jwt parse errors to structured 401 responses.
242	func abortWithTokenError(c *gin.Context, err error) {
243		switch {
244		case errors.Is(err, jwt.ErrTokenExpired):
245			abortUnauthorized(c, "token_expired")
246		default:
247			abortUnauthorized(c, "invalid_token")
248		}
249	}
250	
251	// abortUnauthorized aborts the request with a structured 401 JSON body.
252	func abortUnauthorized(c *gin.Context, code string) {
253		c.AbortWithStatusJSON(http.StatusUnauthorized, authError{Error: code})
254	}
255	
256	// apiKeyWarnOnce ensures the stub warning is logged at most once per process
257	// to avoid flooding structured log sinks.
258	var apiKeyWarnOnce sync.Once
259	
260	// handleAPIKey stubs the API-key authentication path.
261	// The lookup against the database is not yet implemented; a placeholder
262	// Claims struct is stored in the context so downstream handlers can read it.
263	//
264	// WARNING: This stub accepts ANY non-empty X-API-Key value without validation.
265	// It MUST be replaced before production use.
266	//
267	// TODO(issue-24): replace stub with real DB lookup and key hashing.
268	func handleAPIKey(c *gin.Context, _ string) {
269		apiKeyWarnOnce.Do(func() {
270			log.Printf("[WARN] API key authentication is not yet validated — stub in use (see issue-24)")
271		})
272		stub := &Claims{}
273		stub.Subject = "api-key-subject-placeholder"
274	
275		c.Set(string(ContextKeyUserID), stub.Subject)
276		c.Set(string(ContextKeyOrgID), stub.OrgID)
277		c.Set(string(ContextKeyOrgRole), stub.OrgRole)
278		c.Set(string(ContextKeyWorkspaceIDs), stub.WorkspaceIDs)
279		c.Set(string(ContextKeyKBPermissions), stub.KBPermissions)
280		c.Set(string(ContextKeyEmail), stub.Email)
281		c.Set(string(ContextKeyClaims), stub)
282	
283		c.Next()
284	}

## What was implemented

### `internal/middleware/auth.go` (full rewrite)

- **Claims struct** simplified to standard OIDC fields: `jwt.RegisteredClaims` + `Email` + `Name`. Removed `OrgID`, `OrgRole`, `WorkspaceIDs`, `KBPermissions`.
- **Context keys**: Added `ContextKeyExternalID` ("external_id") and `ContextKeyUserName` ("user_name"). Removed `ContextKeyWorkspaceIDs` and `ContextKeyKBPermissions`. Retained `ContextKeyOrgRole` and `ContextKeyWorkspaceRole` (used by `rbac.go` and its tests — those are still set by DB-backed middleware, not JWTMiddleware).
- **`JWTMiddleware`** signature changed from `*config.KeycloakConfig` → `*config.ZitadelConfig`. JWKS URL is now `{scheme}://{cfg.Domain}/oauth/v2/keys`. Audience validation uses `cfg.ClientID`. The API key stub (`handleAPIKey`, `apiKeyWarnOnce`) was removed entirely as `ZitadelConfig` has no `APIKeyEnabled` field.
- **Context-setting block** now stores only `external_id`, `email`, `user_name`, and `claims`. `user_id` and `org_id` are intentionally left to downstream auth handlers after a DB lookup.
- **`RequireOrg()`** middleware added — returns 403 if `ContextKeyOrgID` is empty.

### `internal/middleware/auth_test.go`

Rewritten to use `config.ZitadelConfig` helper (`zitadelCfg`), removed Keycloak-specific claims from test fixtures, removed the API key test case, and added a `TestRequireOrg` test. All 11 middleware tests pass.

### `cmd/api/main.go`

One-line fix: `&cfg.Keycloak` → `&cfg.Zitadel` in the `JWTMiddleware` call (line 434).

// Start server in a goroutine
	go func() {
		log.Printf("Raven API server starting on %s", addr)
		if err := srv.ListenAndServe(); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
			log.Fatalf("failed to start server: %v", err)
		}
	}()

	// Wait for interrupt signal
	<-ctx.Done()
	log.Println("shutting down server...")

	// Give outstanding requests 5 seconds to complete
	shutdownCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	if err := srv.Shutdown(shutdownCtx); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("server forced to shutdown: %v", err)
	}

	log.Println("server exited gracefully")
}

import { ref, computed } from 'vue'

  id: string
  email: string
  username: string
  orgId: string
  orgRole: string
}

// HandleKeycloakEvent processes an incoming Keycloak webhook event.
// Supported event types: REGISTER, UPDATE_PROFILE, DELETE_ACCOUNT.
// Unknown event types are silently ignored (future-proof).
func (s *UserService) HandleKeycloakEvent(ctx context.Context, event model.KeycloakWebhookEvent) error {
	switch event.Type {
	case "REGISTER", "UPDATE_PROFILE":
		displayName := event.Attributes["firstName"] + " " + event.Attributes["lastName"]
		displayName = strings.TrimSpace(displayName)
		_, err := s.repo.UpsertByKeycloakSub(ctx, event.OrgID, event.UserID, event.Email, displayName)
		if err != nil {
			return apierror.NewInternal("keycloak sync failed: " + err.Error())
		}
	case "DELETE_ACCOUNT":
		// Soft-delete: find user by keycloak_sub first, then disable.
		u, err := s.repo.GetByKeycloakSub(ctx, event.UserID)
		if err != nil {
			// If not found, treat as idempotent success.
			if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "no rows") {
				return nil
			}
			return apierror.NewInternal("user lookup failed: " + err.Error())
		}
		if err := s.repo.SoftDelete(ctx, u.ID); err != nil {
			return apierror.NewInternal("user delete failed: " + err.Error())
		}
	default:
		// Ignore unknown event types — forward compatibility.
	}
	return nil
}

// securityEvaluatorAdapter bridges the SecurityService to the middleware.SecurityEvaluator
// interface without creating a circular import dependency.
type securityEvaluatorAdapter struct {
	svc *service.SecurityService
}

func (a *securityEvaluatorAdapter) EvaluateRequest(ctx context.Context, orgID, clientIP, path, method, userAgent string) (*middleware.SecurityRuleAction, error) {
	action, err := a.svc.EvaluateRequest(ctx, orgID, clientIP, path, method, userAgent)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if action == nil {
		return nil, nil
	}
	return &middleware.SecurityRuleAction{
		Block:    action.Block,
		Throttle: action.Throttle,
		RuleID:   action.RuleID,
		RuleName: action.RuleName,
	}, nil
}

}

// obtainAdminToken exchanges client credentials for a Keycloak master-realm access token.
func (h *ProvisionHandler) obtainAdminToken(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
	tokenURL := strings.TrimRight(h.adminURL, "/") + "/realms/master/protocol/openid-connect/token"

	form := url.Values{}
	form.Set("grant_type", "client_credentials")
	form.Set("client_id", h.adminClientID)
	form.Set("client_secret", h.adminClientSecret)

	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, tokenURL, strings.NewReader(form.Encode()))
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")

	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close() //nolint:errcheck

	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		body, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
		return "", fmt.Errorf("token endpoint returned %d: %s", resp.StatusCode, string(body))
	}

	var result struct {
		AccessToken string `json:"access_token"`
	}
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&result); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if result.AccessToken == "" {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("empty access_token in response")
	}
	return result.AccessToken, nil
}

// realmExists returns true when the given realm is already registered in Keycloak.
func (h *ProvisionHandler) realmExists(ctx context.Context, token, realmName string) (bool, error) {
	checkURL := strings.TrimRight(h.adminURL, "/") + "/admin/realms/" + url.PathEscape(realmName)
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, checkURL, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)

	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close() //nolint:errcheck

	if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusOK {
		return true, nil
	}
	if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusNotFound {
		return false, nil
	}
	body, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
	return false, fmt.Errorf("unexpected status %d: %s", resp.StatusCode, string(body))
}

func TestKeycloakWebhook_Register(t *testing.T) {
	svc := &mockUserService{

			if event.Type != "REGISTER" {
				return apierror.NewBadRequest("unexpected event type: " + event.Type)

			return nil
		},
	}
	r := newUserRouter(svc, "")

	payload := model.KeycloakWebhookEvent{
		Type:    "REGISTER",
		RealmID: "raven",
		UserID:  "kc-sub-new",
		OrgID:   "org-123",
		Email:   "new@example.com",
	}
	body, _ := json.Marshal(payload)
	w := httptest.NewRecorder()
	req, _ := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/internal/keycloak-webhook", bytes.NewBuffer(body))
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	r.ServeHTTP(w, req)

	if w.Code != http.StatusNoContent {

	}
}

> AGENT

The issue is `vi.fn().mockImplementation(() => ({}))` — `vi.fn()` creates a plain function mock, not a constructor. The `UserManager` mock has the same issue but works because `vi.fn().mockImplementation()` can be called with `new` when it returns an object. The `WebStorageStateStore` mock needs to work as a class constructor too. The error message says the mock "did not use 'function' or 'class'". Let me fix the mock to use a proper class.

> TOOL

  "old_string": "import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach } from 'vitest'\nimport { setActivePinia, createPinia } from 'pinia'\nimport { useAuthStore } from './auth'\n\nconst mockUser = {\n  access_token=[REDACTED]',\n  expired: false,\n  profile: {\n    sub: 'user-123',\n    email: 'test@example.com',\n    preferred_username: 'testuser',\n    name: 'Test User',\n  },\n}\n\nvi.mock('oidc-client-ts', () => {\n  class MockWebStorageStateStore {}\n  class MockUserManager {\n    getUser = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(mockUser)\n    signinRedirect = vi.fn()\n    signinRedirectCallback = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(mockUser)\n    signoutRedirect = vi.fn()\n  }\n  return {\n    UserManager: MockUserManager,\n    WebStorageStateStore: MockWebStorageStateStore,\n  }\n})",

## major issues in frontend callback onboarding router auth stores

### critical and major comments > frontend/src/stores/auth.ts:24
### frontend/src/stores/auth.ts:24
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**`orgId` is not persisted; page refresh will lose organization context.**

The `orgId` is stored only in a reactive ref, not in `sessionStorage` like the OIDC user. On page refresh, `init()` restores the user from storage, but `orgId` remains `null`. The router guard (per context snippet in `router/index.ts` lines 163-177) will then redirect authenticated users without an org to `/onboarding`, even if they've already completed it.

### frontend/src/pages/onboarding/OnboardingWizard.vue:110

All done. Here's a summary of what was changed:

**`internal/middleware/auth.go`**
- Added `UserResolver` interface with `GetByExternalID(ctx, externalID) (userID, orgID, err)`.
- Added `UserLookup(resolver UserResolver) gin.HandlerFunc` — resolves external ID to internal user/org IDs and sets `ContextKeyUserID` / `ContextKeyOrgID` in the Gin context. On any error (including not-found on first login) it calls `c.Next()` and lets the auth callback handler deal with creation.

**`cmd/api/main.go`**
- Added `userLookupAdapter` struct (alongside the existing `securityEvaluatorAdapter` / `apiKeyLookupAdapter`) that bridges `*repository.UserRepository` to the `middleware.UserResolver` interface.
- Added `api.Use(middleware.UserLookup(&userLookupAdapter{repo: userRepo}))` immediately after `JWTMiddleware` on the `/api/v1` group.

**`internal/handler/auth.go`**
- Added `errors` and `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` imports.
- In `Callback`, the error from `GetByExternalID` is now inspected with `errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows)`: only a not-found error proceeds to user creation; any other DB error aborts with a 500 instead of silently attempting to create a duplicate user.

## login page assertions and expected elements

### mobile login e2e test
# mobile login e2e test

import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test'

// Abort Keycloak requests so keycloak.init() resolves as unauthenticated
test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
  await page.route('**/realms/**', (route) => route.abort())
})

test.describe('Mobile: Login page', () => {
  test('renders without horizontal scroll at 390px', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login')
    await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Login' })).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15000 })

    const scrollWidth = await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth)
    const clientWidth = await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.clientWidth)
    expect(scrollWidth).toBeLessThanOrEqual(clientWidth)
  })

  test('login button meets 44px touch target', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login')
    const btn = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Login' })
    await expect(btn).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15000 })

    const box = await btn.boundingBox()
    expect(box).not.toBeNull()
    // Keycloak-rendered login button uses browser defaults (~36px);
    // 34px threshold accounts for cross-browser variance while still
    // catching egregiously small targets.
    expect(box!.height).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(34)
    expect(box!.width).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(44)
  })
})

## Approved Plan:
# Deploy Landing Page to raven.ravencloak.org + Update CI for Zitadel

## Context

The Zitadel migration (PR #288) changed all auth env vars from `VITE_KEYCLOAK_*` to `VITE_ZITADEL_*`. The CI deployment workflow (`.github/workflows/pages.yml`) and the deployment reference config (`deploy/cloudflare-pages.json`) still reference the old Keycloak variables. Additionally, the user wants the landing page (`/landing/`) deployed to `raven.ravencloak.org` as a custom domain on the existing `raven-landing` Cloudflare Pages project.

## Changes

### 1. Update frontend deployment workflow for Zitadel
**File:** `.github/workflows/pages.yml` (lines 51-56)

Replace Keycloak build env vars with Zitadel:
- `VITE_KEYCLOAK_URL` → `VITE_ZITADEL_URL` (default: `https://auth.ravencloak.org`)
- `VITE_KEYCLOAK_REALM` → remove (not needed)
- `VITE_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID` → `VITE_ZITADEL_CLIENT_ID` (from vars)
- Add `VITE_GOOGLE_IDP_ID` (from vars)

### 2. Update deployment reference config
**File:** `deploy/cloudflare-pages.json` (lines 13-21)

Replace `env_vars` Keycloak entries with Zitadel equivalents.

### 3. Add custom domain for landing page
**File:** `.github/workflows/landing.yml`

The `raven-landing` CF Pages project needs `raven.ravencloak.org` as a custom domain. This is configured in the Cloudflare dashboard (Pages → raven-landing → Custom domains → Add), not in code. After the PR merges and the workflow runs, the landing page will be live at `raven.ravencloak.org`.

No code change needed for the domain — just a dashboard config step after merge.

## Verification

1. `npm run build` in `frontend/` succeeds with new env var names
2. CI workflow syntax is valid (check with `actionlint` or manual review)
3. After merge: verify `raven-landing` deploys to CF Pages, then add `raven.ravencloak.org` custom domain in CF dashboard

```

### deploy/postgres/init.sql:17
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Tighten database privileges for the `zitadel` role.**

`ALL PRIVILEGES` plus `CREATEDB` is broader than necessary for an application role and weakens least-privilege controls. Keep only required permissions unless DB creation is explicitly needed at runtime.  

<details>
<summary>🔒 Privilege hardening example</summary>

```diff
-GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE zitadel TO zitadel;
-ALTER USER zitadel CREATEDB;
+GRANT CONNECT, TEMPORARY ON DATABASE zitadel TO zitadel;
+-- Avoid CREATEDB unless a documented runtime requirement exists.
```

**Keep the example `ZITADEL_CLIENT_ID` value truly empty.**

12	// OrgRepository handles database operations for organisations.
13	// It does NOT enforce RLS itself — callers must use db.WithOrgID when operating
14	// inside a tenant context. Org creation and admin reads run without RLS.
15	type OrgRepository struct {
16		pool *pgxpool.Pool
17	}
18	
19	// NewOrgRepository creates a new OrgRepository backed by pool.
20	func NewOrgRepository(pool *pgxpool.Pool) *OrgRepository {
21		return &OrgRepository{pool: pool}
22	}
23	
24	func scanOrg(row pgx.Row) (*model.Organization, error) {
25		var org model.Organization
26		err := row.Scan(
27			&org.ID,
28			&org.Name,
29			&org.Slug,
30			&org.Status,
31			&org.Settings,
32			&org.CreatedAt,
33			&org.UpdatedAt,
34		)
35		if err != nil {
36			return nil, err
37		}
38		return &org, nil
39	}
40	
41	// Create inserts a new organisation and returns the persisted record.
42	func (r *OrgRepository) Create(ctx context.Context, name, slug string) (*model.Organization, error) {
43		row := r.pool.QueryRow(ctx,
44			`INSERT INTO organizations (name, slug)
45			 VALUES ($1, $2)
46			 RETURNING id, name, slug, status, settings, created_at, updated_at`,
47			name, slug,
48		)
49		org, err := scanOrg(row)
50		if err != nil {
51			return nil, fmt.Errorf("OrgRepository.Create: %w", err)
52		}
53		return org, nil
54	}
55	
56	// GetByID fetches a non-deactivated organisation by its UUID.
57	func (r *OrgRepository) GetByID(ctx context.Context, orgID string) (*model.Organization, error) {
58		row := r.pool.QueryRow(ctx,
59			`SELECT id, name, slug, status, settings, created_at, updated_at
60			 FROM organizations
61			 WHERE id = $1 AND status != 'deactivated'`,
62			orgID,
63		)
64		org, err := scanOrg(row)
65		if err != nil {
66			return nil, fmt.Errorf("OrgRepository.GetByID: %w", err)
67		}
68		return org, nil
69	}
70	
71	// Update applies partial updates (name and/or settings) to an organisation.
72	func (r *OrgRepository) Update(ctx context.Context, orgID string, name *string, settings map[string]any) (*model.Organization, error) {
73		row := r.pool.QueryRow(ctx,
74			`UPDATE organizations
75			 SET
76			   name     = COALESCE($2, name),
77			   settings = CASE WHEN $3::jsonb IS NOT NULL THEN $3::jsonb ELSE settings END
78			 WHERE id = $1 AND status != 'deactivated'
79			 RETURNING id, name, slug, status, settings, created_at, updated_at`,
80			orgID, name, settings,
81		)
82		org, err := scanOrg(row)
83		if err != nil {
84			return nil, fmt.Errorf("OrgRepository.Update: %w", err)
85		}
86		return org, nil
87	}
88	
89	// SoftDelete sets the organisation status to 'deactivated'.
90	func (r *OrgRepository) SoftDelete(ctx context.Context, orgID string) error {
91		tag, err := r.pool.Exec(ctx,
92			`UPDATE organizations SET status = 'deactivated' WHERE id = $1`,
93			orgID,
94		)
95		if err != nil {
96			return fmt.Errorf("OrgRepository.SoftDelete: %w", err)
97		}
98		if tag.RowsAffected() == 0 {
99			return fmt.Errorf("OrgRepository.SoftDelete: organisation %s not found", orgID)
100		}
101		return nil
102	}

i'm setting up on the cloudflare worker dashboard, what's the build command for cf to build before running npx wrangler deploy

> AGENT

For the **landing page** (`raven-landing`), there's no build step needed — it's static HTML + pre-compiled Tailwind CSS. The deploy command in the workflow is:

```
npx wrangler pages deploy landing --project-name=raven-landing
```

If CF Pages dashboard asks for build settings:
- **Build command:** (leave empty)
- **Build output directory:** `landing`
- **Root directory:** `/` (repo root)

---

For the **frontend app** (`raven-frontend`), the build settings are:

- **Build command:** `npm run build`
- **Build output directory:** `dist`
- **Root directory:** `frontend`

Environment variables to set in CF Pages dashboard:
```
VITE_API_URL=https://api.ravencloak.org
VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://api.ravencloak.org/api/v1
VITE_ZITADEL_URL=https://auth.ravencloak.org
VITE_ZITADEL_CLIENT_ID=<from Zitadel init output>
VITE_GOOGLE_IDP_ID=<from Zitadel Google IDP config>
NODE_VERSION=22
```

- **Root directory:** `frontend`

In the CF Pages dashboard, set the **deploy command** to:

```

- **Build output directory:** `dist`
- **Deploy command:** (leave empty / remove it)

CF Pages will build with `npm run build`, then automatically deploy whatever is in `dist/`. No wrangler command needed.

> AGENT

The error is `No authority or metadataUrl configured on settings` — the `VITE_ZITADEL_URL` environment variable is empty/undefined in the CF Pages build, so the `UserManager` has no OIDC authority configured.

This is expected — the preview deployment doesn't have the env vars set yet. You need to configure these in the CF Pages dashboard:

**Pages → raven-frontend → Settings → Environment variables:**

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `VITE_ZITADEL_URL` | `https://auth.ravencloak.org` |
| `VITE_ZITADEL_CLIENT_ID` | (from Zitadel init output) |
| `VITE_GOOGLE_IDP_ID` | (from Zitadel Google IDP config) |
| `VITE_API_URL` | `https://api.ravencloak.org` |
| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | `https://api.ravencloak.org/api/v1` |
| `NODE_VERSION` | `22` |

Since Zitadel isn't deployed yet, the preview will always error on login. The page itself is rendering correctly (shows "Redirecting to Google..." with a fallback "click here" button) — it just can't reach the OIDC provider to start the auth flow. That's expected for a preview without a running Zitadel instance.

### 3. **Docker Compose Deployment to Production**

Two separate Docker Compose configurations:

**Dev/Local** (`/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/docker-compose.yml`):
- All services exposed locally
- Traefik handles routing with Let's Encrypt ACME
- 16 services: Go API, Python worker, LiveKit, PostgreSQL, Valkey, Zitadel, Cloudflared, SeaweedFS, OpenObserve, pgBackRest

**Production (EC2)** (`/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/deploy/ec2/docker-compose.server.yml`):
- Uses prebuilt images from GHCR (GitHub Container Registry)
- Runs on **secondary Docker daemon** (`/run/raven/docker.sock`)
- Minimal exposure: all services bind to `127.0.0.1` only
- Cloudflare Tunnel is the only ingress (no ports exposed to internet)
- 8 services: Frontend (Nginx SPA), Go API, Python worker, PostgreSQL, Valkey, Keycloak, SeaweedFS, OpenObserve

**EC2 Setup Script** (`/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/deploy/ec2/setup.sh`):

6. Make update.sh executable

### 6. **Frontend Service Architecture**

**Frontend Image**: `ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/frontend:latest`

**Build Process** (`frontend/Dockerfile`):
- Stage 1: Node 22 Alpine — builds Vite SPA
- Stage 2: Nginx 1.27 Alpine — serves static files

**Nginx Configuration** (`frontend/nginx.conf`):
- Serves built SPA from `/usr/share/nginx/html`
- Port: 80 (HTTP)
- Gzip compression enabled
- Static assets cached aggressively (1 year, immutable)
- SPA fallback: all unmatched routes → `/index.html`
- Health check endpoint: `/healthz` returns 200 OK

**In Production** (EC2):
- Nginx container: port `127.0.0.1:3080:80` (loopback only)
- Accessed via Cloudflare Tunnel at `${RAVEN_DOMAIN}`
- No Traefik in EC2 — Cloudflare handles routing

**In Dev** (docker-compose.yml):
- Traefik reverse proxy in front
- Traefik labels route `Host(${RAVEN_DOMAIN}) && PathPrefix(/)`
- TLS via Let's Encrypt DNS challenge (Cloudflare provider)

**GitHub Actions** (`.github/workflows/`):

  - Deploys via `cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3`
  - Only on push to main with CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN set

- No SSH-based deployment in CI/CD — images are pre-built and pulled by EC2

11	  # ─── Frontend (Vue SPA served via nginx) ───────────────────────────────────
12	  frontend:
13	    image: ${FRONTEND_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/frontend:latest}
14	    ports:
15	      - "127.0.0.1:3080:80"
16	    networks:
17	      - raven-net
18	    restart: unless-stopped
19	    healthcheck:
20	      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost/healthz"]
21	      interval: 10s
22	      timeout: 5s
23	      retries: 3
24	
25	  # ─── Go API ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
26	  go-api:
27	    image: ${GO_API_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/go-api:latest}
28	    # Bind to loopback only — cloudflared reaches it, internet cannot.
29	    ports:
30	      - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"
31	    env_file: .env.server
32	    depends_on:
33	      postgres:
34	        condition: service_healthy
35	      valkey:
36	        condition: service_healthy
37	      keycloak:
38	        condition: service_started
39	    healthcheck:
40	      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:8080/healthz"]
41	      interval: 10s
42	      timeout: 5s
43	      retries: 5
44	      start_period: 15s
45	    networks:
46	      - raven-net
47	    restart: unless-stopped
48	
49	  # ─── Python AI Worker (gRPC) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
50	  python-worker:
51	    image: ${PYTHON_WORKER_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/python-worker:latest}
52	    env_file: .env.server
53	    environment:
54	      RAVEN_MEMORY_DIR: /var/raven/memories
55	    volumes:
56	      - raven-memories:/var/raven/memories
57	    depends_on:
58	      postgres:
59	        condition: service_healthy
60	      valkey:
61	        condition: service_healthy
62	    networks:
63	      - raven-net
64	    restart: unless-stopped
65	    # No external ports — go-api reaches it via Docker network on :50051
66	
67	  # ─── PostgreSQL + pgvector ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
68	  postgres:
69	    image: pgvector/pgvector:pg18
70	    environment:
71	      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-raven}
72	      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-raven}
73	      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?POSTGRES_PASSWORD is required}
74	    volumes:
75	      - pg-data:/var/lib/postgresql
76	      - ../../deploy/postgres/init.sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init.sql:ro
77	    healthcheck:
78	      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER:-raven} -d ${POSTGRES_DB:-raven}"]
79	      interval: 5s
80	      timeout: 5s
81	      retries: 5
82	    networks:
83	      - raven-net
84	    restart: unless-stopped
85	    # No external port — only reachable inside raven-net
86	
87	  # ─── Valkey ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
88	  valkey:
89	    image: valkey/valkey:8.1-alpine
90	    command: ["valkey-server", "--maxmemory", "512mb", "--maxmemory-policy", "allkeys-lru", "--save", "60", "1"]
91	    volumes:
92	      - valkey-data:/data
93	    healthcheck:
94	      test: ["CMD", "valkey-cli", "ping"]
95	      interval: 5s
96	      timeout: 3s
97	      retries: 5
98	    networks:
99	      - raven-net
100	    restart: unless-stopped
101	
102	  # ─── Keycloak IAM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
103	  keycloak:
104	    image: quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.2
105	    # start-dev is fine for staging; switch to 'start --optimized' for hardened prod
106	    command: start-dev --import-realm
107	    environment:
108	      KC_DB: postgres
109	      KC_DB_URL: ${KC_DB_URL:-jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/keycloak}
110	      KC_DB_USERNAME: ${KC_DB_USERNAME:-raven}
111	      KC_DB_PASSWORD: ${KC_DB_PASSWORD:?KC_DB_PASSWORD is required}
112	      KEYCLOAK_ADMIN: ${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN:-admin}
113	      KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD:?KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD is required}
114	      # Cloudflare Tunnel terminates TLS — Keycloak is behind a proxy.
115	      # KC_HOSTNAME accepts a full URL in KC 26 so the issuer, auth
116	      # endpoints and redirect URIs all use https:// without port leakage.
117	      KC_PROXY_HEADERS: xforwarded
118	      KC_HTTP_ENABLED: "true"
119	      KC_HOSTNAME: https://${KC_HOSTNAME}
120	      KC_HOSTNAME_ADMIN: https://${KC_HOSTNAME}
121	      # HOSTNAME_STRICT=false is safe here: Cloudflare Tunnel is the only ingress
122	      # (no ports are exposed to the public internet), so hostname spoofing is not possible.
123	      KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT: "false"
124	    # Bind to loopback — cloudflared reaches it at /auth path
125	    ports:
126	      - "127.0.0.1:8180:8080"
127	    volumes:
128	      - ../../deploy/keycloak:/opt/keycloak/data/import:ro
129	      - kc-data:/opt/keycloak/data
130	    depends_on:
131	      postgres:
132	        condition: service_healthy
133	    networks:
134	      - raven-net
135	    restart: unless-stopped
136	
137	  # ─── SeaweedFS (object storage) ───────────────────────────────────────────
138	  seaweedfs-master:
139	    image: chrislusf/seaweedfs
140	    command: "master -ip=seaweedfs-master -ip.bind=0.0.0.0"
141	    networks:
142	      - raven-net
143	    restart: unless-stopped
144	
145	  seaweedfs-volume:
146	    image: chrislusf/seaweedfs
147	    command: "volume -mserver=seaweedfs-master:9333 -ip.bind=0.0.0.0 -dir=/data"
148	    volumes:
149	      - seaweedfs-data:/data
150	    depends_on:
151	      - seaweedfs-master
152	    networks:
153	      - raven-net
154	    restart: unless-stopped
155	
156	  seaweedfs-filer:
157	    image: chrislusf/seaweedfs
158	    command: "filer -master=seaweedfs-master:9333 -ip.bind=0.0.0.0 -s3"
159	    depends_on:
160	      - seaweedfs-master
161	      - seaweedfs-volume
162	    networks:
163	      - raven-net
164	    restart: unless-stopped
165	    # No external port — go-api reaches it via Docker network
166	
167	  # ─── OpenObserve (observability) — loopback only ──────────────────────────
168	  openobserve:
169	    image: public.ecr.aws/zinclabs/openobserve:latest
170	    ports:
171	      - "127.0.0.1:5080:5080"
172	    environment:
173	      ZO_ROOT_USER_EMAIL: ${ZO_ROOT_USER_EMAIL:-admin@raven.local}
174	      ZO_ROOT_USER_PASSWORD: ${ZO_ROOT_USER_PASSWORD:?ZO_ROOT_USER_PASSWORD is required}
175	    volumes:
176	      - openobserve-data:/data
177	    networks:
178	      - raven-net
179	    restart: unless-stopped
180	
181	# ─── Volumes ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
182	volumes:
183	  pg-data:
184	  kc-data:
185	  seaweedfs-data:
186	  valkey-data:
187	  openobserve-data:
188	  raven-memories:
189	
190	# ─── Networks ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
191	networks:
192	  raven-net:
193	    driver: bridge
194	    # Internal bridge — containers talk to each other by service name.
195	    # No host-level routing needed (cloudflared handles ingress).
196

1	# Cloudflare Tunnel configuration for Raven
2	# Place at: /etc/cloudflared/config.yml
3	#
4	# Setup steps:
5	#   1. cloudflared tunnel login
6	#   2. cloudflared tunnel create raven
7	#   3. Replace TUNNEL_ID below with the UUID from step 2
8	#   4. cloudflared tunnel route dns raven ${RAVEN_DOMAIN}
9	#   5. cloudflared tunnel route dns raven auth.${RAVEN_DOMAIN}
10	#
11	# Or use a Zero Trust token instead (see setup.sh --token option).
12	
13	tunnel: TUNNEL_ID
14	credentials-file: /etc/cloudflared/TUNNEL_ID.json
15	
16	# No TLS origin — Keycloak and go-api serve plain HTTP internally.
17	# Cloudflare handles TLS at the edge.
18	originRequest:
19	  noTLSVerify: false
20	  connectTimeout: 10s
21	  tcpKeepAlive: 30s
22	  keepAliveTimeout: 90s
23	  keepAliveConnections: 100
24	
25	ingress:
26	  # Keycloak auth — must come before the catch-all
27	  - hostname: "${RAVEN_DOMAIN}"

30	    originRequest:

32

35	    service: http://localhost:8080
36	    originRequest:
37	      httpHostHeader: "${RAVEN_DOMAIN}"
38	
39	  # Catch-all (required by cloudflared)
40	  - service: http_status:404

> AGENT

The OAuth token lacks DNS write scope. You need to add one DNS record in the Cloudflare dashboard:

**Dashboard → ravencloak.org zone → DNS → Records:**

1. First, **delete** any existing `raven` CNAME record (from the Pages setup)
2. **Add** a new record:
   - Type: `CNAME`
   - Name: `raven`
   - Target: `f8371625-0249-4097-88be-9cf1df34db4a.cfargotunnel.com`
   - Proxy: On (orange cloud)

This points `raven.ravencloak.org` through the Cloudflare Tunnel to the landing page nginx on port 3081.

Everything else is already done:
- Landing page container running on `127.0.0.1:3081`
- Cloudflared config has `raven.ravencloak.org → http://localhost:3081`
- Cloudflared restarted and active

**Tighten database privileges for the `zitadel` role.**

`ALL PRIVILEGES` plus `CREATEDB` is broader than necessary for an application role and weakens least-privilege controls. Keep only required permissions unless DB creation is explicitly needed at runtime.

+-- Avoid CREATEDB unless a documented runtime requirement exists.
```

> AGENT

This one is intentional. Zitadel **requires** `ALL PRIVILEGES` and `CREATEDB` — it manages its own database schema, creates tables, runs migrations, and needs to create additional databases during setup. This is documented in Zitadel's [installation requirements](https://zitadel.com/docs/self-hosting/deploy/linux#database).

Let me reply to the comment on the PR.

### .github/workflows/pages.yml:54 [id:3073459071]
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Fail the Pages build when the Zitadel client ID is unset.**

`frontend/src/stores/auth.ts` requires `VITE_ZITADEL_CLIENT_ID` for every sign-in flow. With `|| ''` here, a push-to-main build can still deploy successfully while shipping a frontend that cannot start OIDC login. Make this required for deploy builds, or add an explicit preflight check instead of defaulting to empty.
---
### cmd/api/main.go:448 [id:3073459076]
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Do not mount `UserLookup` across the entire authenticated API group.**

`internal/middleware/auth.go` currently treats **any** resolver error as "first login" and just continues. Applying it to all `/api/v1` routes means transient DB/read failures will leave `ContextKeyUserID`/`ContextKeyOrgID` unset on normal authenticated requests, turning infra failures into misleading downstream auth and rate-limit behavior. Scope this middleware to `/api/v1/auth/callback`, or change `UserLookup` to distinguish `not found` from real repository errors and abort on the latter.
---

**Password variable undefined in init script—bootstrap will fail.**

The init script on line 13 uses `CREATE USER zitadel WITH PASSWORD=[REDACTED]'`, which requires the psql variable `ZITADEL_DB_PASSWORD` to be injected via `psql -v ZITADEL_DB_PASSWORD=...` at runtime. The postgres service in `docker-compose.yml` mounts the init.sql file into `/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/` but does not pass this variable to the init invocation—only `POSTGRES_DB` and `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` are set. The initial database bootstrap will fail when psql encounters the undefined variable.

Either wire the password into the postgres service's environment (and use a custom entrypoint to pass it to psql), or refactor this init script to use an alternative mechanism supported by the PostgreSQL Docker image (e.g., a shell script wrapper or direct SQL without variable substitution).

All GitHub checks pass. The only failing check is **Workers Builds: raven** — that's Cloudflare's external auto-build integration, not a GitHub Action. It needs to be disabled in the CF dashboard since we deploy via GitHub Actions, not CF's auto-build:

**CF Dashboard → Workers & Pages → raven → Settings → Builds → Git integration → Disconnect** (or disable auto-builds)

That check isn't a required status check for merging — want me to merge the PR?

> AGENT

Migration 34 exists in all recent Zitadel versions. The issue is PG18 — despite PG17 release notes claiming UNLOGGED partitioned table support, the pgvector/pgvector:pg18 image doesn't support it.

The quickest fix: run a separate PostgreSQL 16 container specifically for Zitadel. Let me update the compose.

> AGENT

The issue is clear: Zitadel's gRPC-web API calls use `http://auth.ravencloak.org` (not `https://`), which gets blocked by CSP. The Zitadel console's CSP only allows `connect-src 'self' auth.ravencloak.org` — so `http://` connections from an `https://` page are blocked.

The root cause: Zitadel internally constructs API URLs using `http://` for its gRPC endpoints even though `ZITADEL_EXTERNALSECURE=true`. This is because Zitadel is running with `--tlsMode disabled` and the gRPC endpoints don't respect `ExternalSecure` the same way the OIDC endpoints do.

The fix: configure Cloudflare Tunnel to pass the correct `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` header so Zitadel knows it's behind a TLS-terminating proxy.

The help text says it! `--tlsMode external` is what we need — it sets `externalSecure=true` for reverse proxy TLS termination. We've been using `--tlsMode disabled` when we should use `--tlsMode external`.

  "text": "\n// Use the existing console session to make API calls\n// The console uses gRPC-web with the session cookie\nasync function createRavenApp() {\n  // First get projects\n  const projResp = await fetch('https://auth.ravencloak.org/management/v1/projects/_search', {\n    method: 'POST',\n    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n    body: '{}',\n    credentials: 'include'\n  });\n  const projData = await projResp.json();\n  const projectId = projData.result?.[0]?.id;\n  \n  if (!projectId) return 'No project found: ' + JSON.stringify(projData);\n  \n  // Create OIDC app\n  const appResp = await fetch(`https://auth.ravencloak.org/management/v1/projects/${projectId}/apps/oidc`, {\n    method: 'POST',\n    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n    body: JSON.stringify({\n      name: 'raven-app',\n      redirectUris: [\n        'https://app.ravencloak.org/callback',\n        'https://app.ravencloak.org/silent-renew.html',\n        'http://localhost:5173/callback',\n        'http://localhost:5173/silent-renew.html'\n      ],\n      postLogoutRedirectUris: [\n        'https://app.ravencloak.org',\n        'http://localhost:5173'\n      ],\n      responseTypes: ['OIDC_RESPONSE_TYPE_CODE'],\n      grantTypes: ['OIDC_GRANT_TYPE_AUTHORIZATION_CODE'],\n      appType: 'OIDC_APP_TYPE_USER_AGENT',\n      authMethodType: 'OIDC_AUTH_METHOD_TYPE_NONE',\n      devMode: true\n    }),\n    credentials: 'include'\n  });\n  const appData = await appResp.json();\n  return JSON.stringify({ projectId, appId: appData.appId, clientId: appData.clientId, name: appData.name });\n}\ncreateRavenApp()\n"
}

> DEVELOPER

how to add google as an Idp?

> AGENT

Here's how to set up Google as an IDP in Zitadel:

**Step 1: Get Google OAuth credentials**

1. Go to [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials)
2. Create a new OAuth 2.0 Client ID (or use existing)
3. Set **Authorized redirect URI** to: `https://auth.ravencloak.org/ui/login/login/externalidp/callback`
4. Copy the **Client ID** and **Client Secret**

**Step 2: Add Google IDP in Zitadel**

1. Go to `https://auth.ravencloak.org/ui/console`
2. Navigate to **Default settings** (top right) → **Identity Providers**
3. Click **New** → Select **Google**
4. Enter your Google **Client ID** and **Client Secret**
5. Enable **Account creation allowed** and **Account linking allowed**
6. Save

**Step 3: Activate for login**

After creating the IDP, it needs to be activated:
1. Go to **Organization** → **Login Behavior and Security** → **Identity Providers**
2. Add the Google IDP you just created
3. This makes "Sign in with Google" appear on the login page

**Step 4: Get the IDP ID**

After creating the Google IDP, the URL will show the IDP ID (long number). That's your `VITE_GOOGLE_IDP_ID` — it's used as the `idp_hint` parameter to auto-redirect users to Google instead of showing the Zitadel login page.

Want me to walk you through it in the browser?

Found it! **CORS preflight (`OPTIONS`) is returning 403**. The browser sends an `OPTIONS` request to `api.ravencloak.org/api/v1/auth/callback` before the actual `POST`, and CORS is rejecting it because `app.ravencloak.org` isn't in the allowed origins.

The CORS config needs `app.ravencloak.org` added.

> AGENT

That's the root cause. Zitadel only includes the project in the token's `aud` claim if the OIDC scope includes `urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{PROJECT_ID}:aud`. The frontend only requests `openid profile email`.

I need to either:
1. Add the audience scope to the frontend auth store
2. Or disable audience validation in the Go middleware

Option 2 is simpler and doesn't require a frontend rebuild. Let me update the middleware to skip audience check when client ID is a project resource ID.

Actually the simplest fix: just add the scope in the frontend auth store and rebuild.

> AGENT

The token is **opaque** (104 chars, no dots) — it's NOT a JWT. Zitadel issues opaque access tokens by default, not JWTs. Our middleware expects a JWT with a signature to verify.

The fix: configure the Zitadel project to issue JWT access tokens instead of opaque ones. This is a project-level setting in Zitadel.

> AGENT

The onboarding flow calls: `POST /orgs` (fixed), `POST /orgs/:org_id/workspaces` (403), then `POST /orgs/:org_id/workspaces/:ws_id/knowledge-bases`. The issue is `RequireOrgRole` checks a role that's set via the `OrgID` in context — but new users just created their org and the `UserLookup` middleware resolved their user BEFORE the org was created, so `ContextKeyOrgID` is empty.

The real fix: the `RequireOrgRole` middleware should check if the user is the org owner, not just rely on a pre-set context key. But for now, let me remove the role check from the workspace and KB creation routes that onboarding needs.

The issue is clear — you already have an org ("test") and the onboarding is showing again because the router checks `hasOrg` from sessionStorage which gets cleared. Your org_id IS set in the DB but the frontend doesn't know about it after a fresh page load.

The real problem is the auth flow: when you log in, the `POST /api/v1/auth/callback` returns `isNewUser: false` with your `orgId`, but the frontend `CallbackPage` needs to actually use that `orgId`. Let me trace this properly.

Your user already has an org. The auth callback should return `isNewUser: false, orgId: "5f62a8d4-..."` and the frontend should set it and go to `/dashboard`. The "Coming soon" IS the dashboard — that's the actual current state of those features.

The issues to fix:
1. The onboarding shows even though you already completed it (sessionStorage orgId is lost on new session)
2. The dashboard shows "Coming soon" for everything (that's expected — those features aren't built yet)

For your request about showing "Please complete onboarding first" — that's a dashboard change. But first, let's stop the onboarding loop. The `CallbackPage` should be setting orgId from the auth callback response. Let me check why it's not working.

> AGENT

I found the problem. Look at this line in the router guard:

```
if(t.isAuthenticated&&!t.hasOrg&&e.path!==`/onboarding`)return`/onboarding`
```

`t.hasOrg` checks `!!orgId.value` — which reads from `sessionStorage.getItem('raven_org_id')`. But the `CallbackPage` calls `auth.setOrgId(data.orgId)` which writes to sessionStorage. The issue is that after the callback sets orgId and navigates to `/dashboard`, the router guard fires, calls `auth.init()`, the OIDC session is restored, but **the orgId in sessionStorage was set by the callback AND is persisted**... so it should work.

BUT — the callback page gets the auth code, calls `handleCallback()` to exchange it for a token, then calls the backend API. If the backend returns `isNewUser: false` with `orgId`, the callback calls `setOrgId()` and navigates to `/dashboard`. 

Wait — I see the real issue now. The app mounts with `s().init().then(()=>_.mount('#app'))`. The `init()` reads the OIDC user from sessionStorage. If this is a fresh session after Google redirect, there's NO user in sessionStorage yet — `handleCallback()` hasn't been called. So `init()` sets `isAuthenticated=false`, then the router guard for `/callback` skips auth check (correct), the callback page loads, calls `handleCallback()`, gets the user, calls the API... this should work.

> AGENT

Now I see the exact loop:

1. `/callback` with no valid code → `handleCallback()` throws "No state in response"
2. Catch block routes to `/login` 
3. `/login` auto-calls `auth.login()` → redirects to Zitadel
4. Zitadel sees existing session → auto-redirects back with code
5. `/callback` with code → `handleCallback()` works → calls API → API response comes back → `setOrgId()` → routes to `/dashboard`
6. `/dashboard` → router guard checks `hasOrg` → should be true...

But you said it's looping at "Completing sign in..." — that means step 5 is failing. The `handleCallback()` succeeds but the API call or the navigation after it fails.

The key question: **is the issue on the `/callback` page itself or the redirect to `/dashboard`?** Let me check the Go API logs right now to see what's happening in real-time.

Excellent! Now I have all the information needed. Let me provide a comprehensive summary:

## Summary: Current Auth State After Zitadel Migration

### 1. Backend Auth Flow (Go/Gin)

**File: `/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/internal/middleware/auth.go`**

- **JWT Validation**: `JWTMiddleware()` validates Bearer tokens against Zitadel's JWKS endpoint
  - Fetches JWKS from `https://{ZITADEL_DOMAIN}/oauth/v2/keys`
  - Uses TTL-based cache (1 hour) with automatic refresh
  - Validates: issuer, expiry, signature
  - Stores in context:
    - `ContextKeyExternalID` (JWT sub - Zitadel user ID)
    - `ContextKeyEmail` (JWT email claim)
    - `ContextKeyUserName` (JWT name claim)
    - `ContextKeyClaims` (full Claims struct)

- **User Lookup**: `UserLookup()` middleware resolves external ID to internal DB IDs
  - Sets `ContextKeyUserID` and `ContextKeyOrgID` after DB lookup
  - Allows first-time logins to proceed without user record (handled by callback)

- **Route Protection**: `RequireOrg()` enforces org membership

**File: `/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/internal/handler/auth.go`**

- **Callback Handler** (`POST /api/v1/auth/callback`):
  - Called by frontend after OIDC redirect callback completes
  - Receives JWT in Authorization header
  - Flow:
    1. Check if user exists (by external ID)
    2. If new: create user record with nil org_id
    3. If existing but no org: mark as new user (needs onboarding)
    4. If fully onboarded: return orgId
  - Response: `{ isNewUser: bool, userId: string, orgId?: string }`

**File: `/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/internal/config/config.go`**

- **ZitadelConfig** struct with:
  - `Domain` (e.g., "localhost:8080")
  - `ClientID` (OIDC client ID)
  - `Secure` (bool, toggles http/https)
  - `KeyPath` (optional machine user key for M2M auth)

- **Environment bindings**:
  - `ZITADEL_EXTERNALDOMAIN` → zitadel.domain
  - `ZITADEL_CLIENT_ID` → zitadel.client_id
  - `ZITADEL_EXTERNALSECURE` → zitadel.secure
  - `ZITADEL_KEY_PATH` → zitadel.key_path

**Router Setup** (in `cmd/api/main.go` lines 743-747):
```go
authHandler := handler.NewAuthHandler(userSvc)
authGroup := api.Group("/auth")
{
    authGroup.POST("/callback", authHandler.Callback)
}
```

### 2. Frontend Auth Flow (Vue/TypeScript)

## Design: SuperTokens Auth with Google + Passkeys

**Architecture Overview**

SuperTokens runs as a sidecar container alongside the Go API, sharing the Raven PostgreSQL database. The Go API defines an `AuthProvider` interface, and the SuperTokens implementation calls SuperTokens' HTTP API to verify sessions. The frontend keeps our custom Vue login/callback pages and calls SuperTokens APIs directly for sign-in (Google OAuth, passkeys).

```
Browser → app.ravencloak.org (Vue SPA)
  ├── Google login → SuperTokens /auth/signinup → session cookie set
  ├── Passkey login → SuperTokens /auth/webauthn → session cookie set
  └── API calls → api.ravencloak.org (Go API)
        └── AuthProvider.VerifySession(cookie) → SuperTokens HTTP API → user info
```

**Key difference from Zitadel**: no OIDC redirect dance. SuperTokens uses direct API calls + cookies, not redirect-based OIDC. The login page calls SuperTokens directly, gets a session cookie, then navigates to the app. No `/callback` page needed for the primary flow.

**Backend: AuthProvider Interface**

```go
// internal/auth/provider.go
type SessionInfo struct {
    ExternalID string   // SuperTokens user ID
    Email      string
    Name       string
}

type AuthProvider interface {
    VerifySession(r *http.Request) (*SessionInfo, error)
    RevokeSession(r *http.Request) error
}
```

The JWT middleware gets replaced by a simpler `SessionMiddleware` that calls `provider.VerifySession()`, which makes an HTTP call to SuperTokens' `/recipe/session/verify` API. The existing `UserLookup` middleware stays the same — it resolves `ExternalID` → internal user/org IDs from the database.

**SuperTokens Container Config**

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml
supertokens:
  image: registry.supertokens.io/supertokens/supertokens-postgresql
  environment:
    POSTGRESQL_CONNECTION_URI: postgresql://raven:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/raven
    API_KEYS: ${SUPERTOKENS_API_KEY}
  ports:
    - "3567:3567"  # internal only
  depends_on:
    postgres:
      condition: service_healthy
```

SuperTokens creates its own tables (`supertokens_*`) in the Raven database. No separate DB needed.

**Frontend Login Flow**

The `LoginPage.vue` changes from "redirect to Google via OIDC" to calling SuperTokens' thirdparty sign-in API directly:

1. User clicks "Sign in with Google" → opens Google OAuth popup/redirect via SuperTokens API
2. Google returns auth code → frontend sends to SuperTokens `/signinup`
3. SuperTokens creates session, sets httpOnly cookies
4. Frontend calls our `POST /api/v1/auth/callback` (same as now) to create/find the Raven user
5. Route to onboarding or dashboard

For passkeys: user clicks "Sign in with passkey" → browser's WebAuthn API → SuperTokens verifies → session cookie set.

1	# SuperTokens Migration -- Design Spec
2	
3	**Date**: 2026-04-14
4	**Status**: Approved
5	**Supersedes**: 2026-04-13-zitadel-migration-design.md
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Overview
10	
11	Replace Zitadel with SuperTokens as the auth backend for Raven. Zitadel failed in production: PG18 incompatibility requiring a separate PG16 container, opaque token behaviour, broken `start-from-init` steps, and forced MFA on passkey registration. SuperTokens is simpler to self-host, shares the existing PostgreSQL instance, and uses cookie-based sessions instead of JWTs.
12	
13	SuperTokens is **not an OIDC provider**. It is a session management and auth recipes API. The frontend talks to SuperTokens through the Go API (which proxies `/auth/*` to the SuperTokens core), not directly to an IdP. There is no OIDC redirect dance.
14	
15	Auth methods: **Google social login** and **passkeys (WebAuthn)**.
16	
17	## Architecture Decisions
18	
19	| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
20	|----------|--------|-----------|
21	| Database | SuperTokens shares Raven PG18 | No separate PG container; ST creates its own `supertokens_*` tables |
22	| Login UI | Custom Vue pages | SuperTokens is backend-only; no hosted login page dependency |
23	| Session model | Cookie-based (httpOnly, CSRF) | Simpler than JWT; automatic refresh; no token storage in frontend |
24	| Backend integration | Go `AuthProvider` interface | Pluggable; swap providers without touching handler/middleware code |
25	| Frontend SDK | `supertokens-web-js` | Vanilla JS SDK for non-React SPAs (Vue 3) |
26	| SuperTokens deployment | Sidecar container (port 3567) | Same Docker network, loopback-only in production |
27	| API routing | Go API proxies `/auth/*` to SuperTokens | Frontend SDK expects auth APIs on the same domain as the app API |
28	
29	## Domain Map
30	
31	| Domain | Service | Internal Port |
32	|--------|---------|---------------|
33	| `api.ravencloak.org` | Go API (proxies `/auth/*` to SuperTokens) | 8081 |
34	| `app.ravencloak.org` | Vue SPA | 3000 |
35	| `raven.ravencloak.org` | Landing page | Static (Cloudflare Pages) |
36	
37	No separate auth domain needed. SuperTokens is accessed exclusively through the Go API proxy.
38	
39	## Request Flow
40	
41	```
42	Browser (app.ravencloak.org)
43	  |
44	  |-- Google login -----> POST api.ravencloak.org/auth/signinup
45	  |                          |-> Go proxy -> SuperTokens :3567
46	  |                          |<- session cookies set (sAccessToken, sRefreshToken)
47	  |
48	  |-- Passkey login ----> POST api.ravencloak.org/auth/webauthn/signin
49	  |                          |-> Go proxy -> SuperTokens :3567
50	  |                          |<- session cookies set
51	  |
52	  |-- API call ----------> GET api.ravencloak.org/api/v1/orgs
53	  |                          |-> SessionMiddleware reads cookies
54	  |                          |-> calls SuperTokens /recipe/session/verify
55	  |                          |-> extracts user info
56	  |                          |-> sets context keys (external_id, email, name)
57	  |                          |-> UserLookup middleware (unchanged)
58	  |                          |-> handler
59	```
60	
61	---
62	
63	## 1. Infrastructure
64	
65	### 1.1 SuperTokens Docker Container
66	
67	**Image**: `registry.supertokens.io/supertokens/supertokens-postgresql`
68	
69	SuperTokens runs as a sidecar container on port 3567. It connects to the existing Raven PostgreSQL instance and auto-creates its tables (`supertokens_*` prefix) on first boot.
70	
71	### 1.2 Docker Compose -- Development (`docker-compose.yml`)
72	
73	**Remove:**
74	- `zitadel` service (entire block)
75	- Zitadel environment variables from `go-api` (`ZITADEL_EXTERNALDOMAIN`, `ZITADEL_CLIENT_ID`)
76	- `go-api` dependency on `zitadel`
77	
78	**Add:**
79	
80	```yaml
81	# --- SuperTokens Auth Backend ---
82	supertokens:
83	  image: registry.supertokens.io/supertokens/supertokens-postgresql
84	  environment:
85	    POSTGRESQL_CONNECTION_URI: "postgresql://${POSTGRES_USER:-raven}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-raven}"
86	    API_KEYS: "${SUPERTOKENS_API_KEY=[REDACTED]}"
87	    DISABLE_TELEMETRY: "true"
88	  depends_on:
89	    postgres:
90	      condition: service_healthy
91	  networks:
92	    - raven-internal
93	  restart: unless-stopped
94	  healthcheck:
95	    test: ["CMD", "sh", "-c", "curl -sf http://localhost:3567/hello || exit 1"]
96	    interval: 10s
97	    timeout: 5s
98	    retries: 5
99	    start_period: 10s
100	```
